Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.

It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

Initialize a StGit stack on a branch.

Initializing a branch with a StGit stack commits initial, empty stack state for the
branch to the repository. Theses stack metadata commits are tracked by the
`refs/stacks/<branch>` reference. Updated stack state is committed by each StGit command
that modifies the stack. StGit users do not have to do anything with the
`refs/stacks/<branch>` ref directly.

Some StGit commands, such as `stg new` and `stg uncommit`, will automatically initialize
the stack, so it is often not necessary to explicitly initialize the stack on a branch.
Also, branches created with `stg branch --create` are automatically initialized.

The branch must already exist and point to a commit before initializing a StGit stack.

StGit stack metadata can be deinitialized from a branch using `stg branch --cleanup`.
See 'stg branch' for more details.

currently applied patches, and is made the new top of the stack. Uncommitted changes in
the work tree are not included in the patch -- that is handled by stg-refresh.

The given patch name must be unique in the stack. If no name is given, one is generated
from the first line of the patch's commit message.

Patch names follow the rules for Git references with the additional constraint that
patch names may not contain the '/' character. See git-check-ref-format(1) for details.

Patch names may start with a leading '-'. When specifying such a patch name on the
command line, the leading '-' may be escaped with a single backslash as in
'\-patch-name' to disambiguate the patch name from command line options.

An editor will be launched to edit the commit message to be used for the patch, unless
the '--message' flag already specified one. The 'patchdescr.tmpl' template file (if
available) is used to pre-fill the editor.

python3 - << 'PY'
import subprocess, json
def git(*a): return subprocess.check_output(["git"]+list(a), text=True)
# walk prev chain
oid=git("rev-parse","refs/stacks/master").strip()
seen=set()
while oid and oid not in seen:
    seen.add(oid)
    print("stackcommit",oid)
    print(git("cat-file","-p",oid))
    try:
        sj=json.loads(git("cat-file","-p",f"{oid}:stack.json"))
        print(" prev=",sj['prev']," head=",sj['head'])
        oid=sj['prev']
    except Exception as e:
        print(e); break
    print()
    if len(seen)>20: break
PY"}

def capture_refresh_tree(repo,stack,target_patch,opts,paths):
    head_oid=stack.head; head_c=Commit(repo,head_oid); head_tree=head_c.tree
    index_mode=bool(opts.get("index")); force=bool(opts.get("force")); update=bool(opts.get("update"))
    check_no_conflicts(repo)
    if not index_mode and not force:
        # index tree vs head, worktree vs index
        p_idx=git_out("write-tree"); idx_tree=p_idx.stdout.decode().strip() if p_idx.returncode==0 else head_tree
        wt_vs_idx=git_out("diff","--quiet").returncode!=0
        if idx_tree!=head_tree and wt_vs_idx:
            raise AppError("the index is dirty; consider using `--index` or `--force`")
    if index_mode:
        p=git_out("write-tree"); return p.stdout.decode().strip()
    # temp index
    fd,tmpindex=tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd); os.unlink(tmpindex)
    env={"GIT_INDEX_FILE":tmpindex}
    try:
        if update:
            git_out("read-tree",head_oid,env=env)
            patch_files=[]
            if target_patch and target_patch in stack.patches:
                pc=stack.patch_commit(target_patch); parent=pc.parents[0] if pc.parents else "4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904"
                p=git_out("diff","--name-only",parent,pc.oid); patch_files=p.stdout.decode().splitlines()
            use_paths=list(paths) if paths else patch_files
            if paths and patch_files:
                # intersect by checking path matches patch file or directory prefix
                filt=[]
                for pf in patch_files:
                    for pa in paths:
                        pa_norm=os.path.normpath(os.path.join(repo.prefix,pa)) if repo.prefix else os.path.normpath(pa)
                        if pf==pa_norm or pf.startswith(pa_norm.rstrip("/")+"/"): filt.append(pf)
                use_paths=filt
            if use_paths:
                git_out("add","-u","--",*use_paths,env=env)
            p=git_out("write-tree",env=env); return p.stdout.decode().strip()
        if paths:
            git_out("read-tree",head_oid,env=env)
            # git add --all for explicit paths (relative to cwd/prefix)
            p=git_out("add","--all","--",*paths,env=env)
            if p.returncode!=0:
                raise AppError(p.stderr.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape').strip())
            p=git_out("write-tree",env=env); return p.stdout.decode().strip()
        # no paths: start from real index
        p_idx=git_out("write-tree"); idx_tree=p_idx.stdout.decode().strip()
        git_out("read-tree",idx_tree,env=env)
        # Update tracked files from worktree across whole repo: run in worktree root
        # git add -u uses cwd pathspec . if in root; use -- with :(top)
        p=git_out("add","-u","--",":/",env=env) if False else run_cmd(["git","add","-u","--","."],cwd=repo.worktree,env=env)
        p=git_out("write-tree",env=env); return p.stdout.decode().strip()
    finally:
        try: os.unlink(tmpindex)
        except OSError: pass

def unique_name(base,existing):
    if base not in existing: return base
    i=1
    while f"{base}-{i}" in existing: i+=1
    return f"{base}-{i}"

def simplified_chain(repo,stack):

    while cur and cur not in seen:
        seen.add(cur)

def capture_refresh_tree(repo,stack,target_patch,opts,paths):
    head_oid=stack.head; head_c=Commit(repo,head_oid); head_tree=head_c.tree
    index_mode=bool(opts.get("index")); force=bool(opts.get("force")); update=bool(opts.get("update"))
    check_no_conflicts(repo)
    if not index_mode and not force:
        # index tree vs head, worktree vs index
        p_idx=git_out("write-tree"); idx_tree=p_idx.stdout.decode().strip() if p_idx.returncode==0 else head_tree
        wt_vs_idx=git_out("diff","--quiet").returncode!=0
        if idx_tree!=head_tree and wt_vs_idx:
            raise AppError("the index is dirty; consider using `--index` or `--force`")
    if index_mode:
        p=git_out("write-tree"); return p.stdout.decode().strip()
    # temp index
    fd,tmpindex=tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd); os.unlink(tmpindex)
    env={"GIT_INDEX_FILE":tmpindex}
    try:
        if update:
            git_out("read-tree",head_oid,env=env)
            patch_files=[]
            if target_patch and target_patch in stack.patches:
                pc=stack.patch_commit(target_patch); parent=pc.parents[0] if pc.parents else "4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904"
                p=git_out("diff","--name-only",parent,pc.oid); patch_files=p.stdout.decode().splitlines()
            use_paths=list(paths) if paths else patch_files
            if paths and patch_files:
                # intersect by checking path matches patch file or directory prefix
                filt=[]
                for pf in patch_files:
                    for pa in paths:
                        pa_norm=os.path.normpath(os.path.join(repo.prefix,pa)) if repo.prefix else os.path.normpath(pa)
                        if pf==pa_norm or pf.startswith(pa_norm.rstrip("/")+"/"): filt.append(pf)
                use_paths=filt
            if use_paths:
                git_out("add","-u","--",*use_paths,env=env)
            p=git_out("write-tree",env=env); return p.stdout.decode().strip()
        if paths:
            git_out("read-tree",head_oid,env=env)
            # git add --all for explicit paths (relative to cwd/prefix)
            p=git_out("add","--all","--",*paths,env=env)
            if p.returncode!=0:
                raise AppError(p.stderr.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape').strip())
            p=git_out("write-tree",env=env); return p.stdout.decode().strip()
        # no paths: start from real index
        p_idx=git_out("write-tree"); idx_tree=p_idx.stdout.decode().strip()
        git_out("read-tree",idx_tree,env=env)
        # Update tracked files from worktree across whole repo: run in worktree root
        # git add -u uses cwd pathspec . if in root; use -- with :(top)
        p=git_out("add","-u","--",":/",env=env) if False else run_cmd(["git","add","-u","--","."],cwd=repo.worktree,env=env)
        p=git_out("write-tree",env=env); return p.stdout.decode().strip()
    finally:
        try: os.unlink(tmpindex)
        except OSError: pass

def unique_name(base,existing):
    if base not in existing: return base
    i=1
    while f"{base}-{i}" in existing: i+=1
    return f"{base}-{i}"

    p=git_out("diff","--full-index",parent,temp_tree)
    return p.stdout.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape')

def do_refresh(repo,stack,parsed_opts,paths,target_override=None):
    # parsed_opts as dict-like Parsed
    opts=parsed_opts.values if hasattr(parsed_opts,'values') else parsed_opts
    def og(k,d=None): return opts.get(k,d) if isinstance(opts,dict) else parsed_opts.get(k,d)
    stack.check_head()
    if target_override: target=target_override
    elif og("patch"):
        target=LocatorResolver(stack).resolve_name(og("patch"))
        if target not in stack.applied:
            # probe message may differ
            raise AppError(f"patch `{target}` is not applied")
    else:
        if not stack.applied: raise AppError("no patches applied")
        target=stack.top()
    # capture tree first (may error dirty)
    temp_tree=capture_refresh_tree(repo,stack,target,opts if isinstance(opts,dict) else parsed_opts,paths)
    temp_name=unique_name("refresh-temp",set(stack.patches.keys()))
    # create temp patch commit
    author_i,committer_i=check_identities(repo)
    temp_oid=create_commit(repo,temp_tree,[stack.head],f"Refresh of {target}",author=author_i,check=False,env_extra={"GIT_COMMITTER_NAME":committer_i.name,"GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL":committer_i.email,"GIT_COMMITTER_DATE":committer_i.git_date()})
    # Trans1
    trans1=Transaction(stack,f"refresh {temp_name} (create temporary patch)"); trans1.worktree_mode="index_only"
    trans1.stack.applied.append(temp_name); trans1.stack.patches[temp_name]=temp_oid; trans1.stack.head=temp_oid
    trans1.ev(f"> {temp_name} (new)"); trans1.commit()
    # Reload stack after trans1
    stack2=Stack.open(repo,stack.branch)
    # Patch description handling (editor etc) happens after temp creation
    old_target_commit=stack2.patch_commit(target)
    desc=None
    edit_opts=dict(opts) if isinstance(opts,dict) else dict(parsed_opts.values)
    # Determine if any patch edit opts present beyond defaults
    has_edit_opts=any(edit_opts.get(k) for k in ["edit","message","file","author","authname","authemail","authdate","signoff","ack","review"]) or edit_opts.get("committer_date_is_author_date")
    diff_text=refresh_desc_diff(repo,stack2,target,temp_tree) if edit_opts.get("diff") else None
    # get desc with editor_by_default False
    edit_opts2=dict(edit_opts); edit_opts2["_editor_by_default"]=False
    desc=get_patch_desc_from_opts(repo,edit_opts2,target,old_target_commit.message,base_commit=old_target_commit,allow_editor=True,diff_text=diff_text)
    # commit-msg hook if message changed or edit opts? Run if has_edit_opts and message differs? Original refresh likely runs hook when updating patch desc. Apply if message/author/tree will create new commit below - defer hook call until commit creations in specific branch
    new_name=desc.name or target
    if new_name!=target:
        r=patch_name_invalid_reason(new_name)
        if r: raise AppError(f"invalid patch name `{new_name}`: {r}")
        if new_name in stack2.patches and new_name!=target: raise AppError(f"patch `{new_name}` already exists")
    # Trans2
    log_msg="refresh" if new_name!=target else f"refresh {target}"
    if og("annotate"):
        log_msg=log_msg+"\n\n"+str(og("annotate"))
    allow_conf=True
    conf=og("conflicts")
    if conf is not None:
        allow_conf = not (conf=="disallow")
    else:
        cfg=repo.config_get("stgit.push.allow-conflicts"); allow_conf = (cfg!="false")
    trans=Transaction(stack2,log_msg,allow_conflicts=allow_conf,committer_date_is_author_date=bool(og("committer_date_is_author_date")))
    # Target position
    applied= list(trans.stack.applied)  # includes temp on top
    t_idx=applied.index(target); above=applied[t_idx+1:-1] if applied and applied[-1]==temp_name else applied[t_idx+1:]
    # If target is immediately below temp (top original)
    if not above:
        # pop temp
        trans.pop_patches_internal([temp_name],record=True)
        # delete temp
        # remove from unapplied & patches
        trans.stack.unapplied=[n for n in trans.stack.unapplied if n!=temp_name]; del trans.stack.patches[temp_name]; trans.ev(f"# {temp_name}")
        # create new target commit if changed
        parent=old_target_commit.parents[0] if old_target_commit.parents else None
        msg=run_commit_msg_hook(repo,desc.message,no_verify=bool(og("no_verify"))) if has_edit_opts else desc.message
        changed=(temp_tree!=old_target_commit.tree or msg!=old_target_commit.message or desc.author.name!=old_target_commit.author.name or desc.author.email!=old_target_commit.author.email or desc.author.ts!=old_target_commit.author.ts or desc.author.tz!=old_target_commit.author.tz)
        if changed:
            parents=[parent] if parent else []
            new_oid=create_commit(repo,temp_tree,parents,msg,author=desc.author,committer_date=(desc.author if og("committer_date_is_author_date") else None))
            trans.stack.patches[target]=new_oid; trans.stack.head=new_oid; trans.ev(f"& {target}")
        else:
            trans.stack.head=old_target_commit.oid
        if new_name!=target:
            # rename in lists/dict
            trans.stack.applied=[new_name if n==target else n for n in trans.stack.applied]
            trans.stack.patches[new_name]=trans.stack.patches.pop(target)
            trans.ev(f"{target} => {new_name}")
        trans.worktree_mode="index_only"
        trans.commit(log_msg)
    else:
        # Non-top
        # pop above+temp
        pop_names=above+[temp_name]
        trans.pop_patches_internal(pop_names,record=True)
        # Push temp onto target
        try:
            ok=trans.push_one_internal(temp_name,record_prefix=">")
        except _DisallowConflict as e:
            raise AppError(f"pushing patch `{e.patch}` would result in conflicts and push conflicts are disallowed",code=3)
        if not ok:
            # conflict on pushing temp
            trans.worktree_mode="checkout"
            # Log message in original: "refresh " (plus CONFLICT added -> two spaces). Set log msg to "refresh " to reproduce?
            trans.commit("refresh ")
            return
        # pop temp
        # capture pushed temp tree (resulting target combined tree)
        pushed_temp_c=Commit(repo,trans.stack.patches[temp_name]); combined_tree=pushed_temp_c.tree
        trans.pop_patches_internal([temp_name],record=True)
        trans.stack.unapplied=[n for n in trans.stack.unapplied if n!=temp_name]; del trans.stack.patches[temp_name]; trans.ev(f"# {temp_name}")
        # modify target
        parent=old_target_commit.parents[0] if old_target_commit.parents else None
        msg=run_commit_msg_hook(repo,desc.message,no_verify=bool(og("no_verify"))) if has_edit_opts else desc.message
        changed=(combined_tree!=old_target_commit.tree or msg!=old_target_commit.message or desc.author.name!=old_target_commit.author.name or desc.author.email!=old_target_commit.author.email or desc.author.ts!=old_target_commit.author.ts)
        if changed:
            new_oid=create_commit(repo,combined_tree,[parent] if parent else [],msg,author=desc.author,committer_date=(desc.author if og("committer_date_is_author_date") else None))
            trans.stack.patches[target]=new_oid; trans.stack.head=new_oid; trans.ev(f"& {target}")
        if new_name!=target:
            trans.stack.applied=[new_name if n==target else n for n in trans.stack.applied]
            trans.stack.unapplied=[new_name if n==target else n for n in trans.stack.unapplied]
            trans.stack.patches[new_name]=trans.stack.patches.pop(target); trans.ev(f"{target} => {new_name}"); target=new_name
        # repush above
        for idx,name in enumerate(above):
            prefix=">" if idx==len(above)-1 else "+"
            try: ok=trans.push_one_internal(name,record_prefix=prefix)
            except _DisallowConflict as e:
                raise AppError(f"pushing patch `{e.patch}` would result in conflicts and push conflicts are disallowed",code=3)
            if not ok:
                trans.worktree_mode="checkout"; trans.commit(log_msg); return
        trans.worktree_mode="checkout"
        trans.commit(log_msg)

def show_one_commit(repo,oid,stat=False,diff_opts=None,paths=None):

        # Our loop gives 4 spaces for empty.
    if stat:
        parent=c.parents[0] if c.parents else "4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904"
        args=["diff","--stat",parent,oid]

    # diff
    parent=c.parents[0] if c.parents else "4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904"

def capture_refresh_tree(repo,stack,target_patch,opts,paths):

            raise AppError("the index is dirty; consider using `--index` or `--force`")

        p=git_out("write-tree"); return p.stdout.decode().strip()

    fd,tmpindex=tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd); os.unlink(tmpindex)
    env={"GIT_INDEX_FILE":tmpindex}

        if update:

                        pa_norm=os.path.normpath(os.path.join(repo.prefix,pa)) if repo.prefix else os.path.normpath(pa)
                        if pf==pa_norm or pf.startswith(pa_norm.rstrip("/")+"/"): filt.append(pf)

            if use_paths:

            if p.returncode!=0:

        p=git_out("add","-u","--",":/",env=env) if False else run_cmd(["git","add","-u","--","."],cwd=repo.worktree,env=env)
        p=git_out("write-tree",env=env); return p.stdout.decode().strip()

        except OSError: pass

def unique_name(base,existing):

    i=1
    while f"{base}-{i}" in existing: i+=1
    return f"{base}-{i}"

# ---------- edit/fold/spill/squash ----------
def apply_diff_to_tree(repo,base_tree,diff_text,strip=1,threeway_base=None):
    # Use temp index, git apply --cached
    fd,tmpindex=tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd); os.unlink(tmpindex); env={"GIT_INDEX_FILE":tmpindex}
    try:
        git_out("read-tree",base_tree,env=env)
        args=["apply","--cached",f"-p{strip}"]
        p=git_out(*args,env=env,inp=diff_text)
        if p.returncode!=0:
            raise AppError(p.stderr.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape').strip() or "failed to apply diff")
        p2=git_out("write-tree",env=env); return p2.stdout.decode().strip()
    finally:
        try: os.unlink(tmpindex)
        except OSError: pass

def cmd_edit(args):
    opts=patch_edit_options(True,True,True)+[Opt("set_tree",long="--set-tree",short="t",value_name="<treeish>"),color_opt()]
    pos=[Pos("patch","[patch]",minv=0,maxv=1,validator=v_patch_locator,allow_hyphen=True)]
    conflicts=edit_conflicts(True,True,True)
    spec=Spec("edit",options=opts,positionals=pos,conflicts=conflicts)
    parsed=parse_args(spec,args); repo=open_repo(); st=Stack.open(repo)
    if parsed.get("patch"): target=LocatorResolver(st).resolve_name(parsed.get("patch"))
    else:
        if not st.applied: raise AppError("no patches applied")
        target=st.top()
    old_c=st.patch_commit(target)
    # diff text for template
    diff_text=None
    if parsed.get("diff"):
        parent_tree=old_c.parent_tree(); p=git_out("diff","--full-index",parent_tree,old_c.tree); diff_text=p.stdout.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape')
    edit_opts=dict(parsed.values); edit_opts["_editor_by_default"]=True; edit_opts["_diff_editable"]=True
    # If any explicit non-editor patch changing options are supplied and -e not set, get_patch_desc will only edit if _editor_by_default AND no file/message. But if e.g. --author only, original does not launch editor. Detect changing opts:
    changing_opts=any(edit_opts.get(k) for k in ["message","file","author","authname","authemail","authdate","signoff","ack","review","set_tree"]) or edit_opts.get("committer_date_is_author_date")
    if changing_opts and not edit_opts.get("edit"): edit_opts["_editor_by_default"]=False
    desc=get_patch_desc_from_opts(repo,edit_opts,target,old_c.message,base_commit=old_c,allow_editor=True,diff_text=diff_text)
    # tree
    new_tree=old_c.tree
    if parsed.get("set_tree"):
        oid=rev_resolve(repo,st,parsed.get("set_tree"))
        p=git_out("rev-parse",oid+"^{tree}"); new_tree=p.stdout.decode().strip()
    elif getattr(desc,'diff',None):
        # If diff edited (or even unedited applying it should yield old tree)
        new_tree=apply_diff_to_tree(repo,old_c.parent_tree(),desc.diff)
    msg=run_commit_msg_hook(repo,desc.message,no_verify=bool(parsed.get("no_verify")))
    new_name=desc.name or target
    if new_name!=target:
        r=patch_name_invalid_reason(new_name)
        if r: raise AppError(f"invalid patch name `{new_name}`: {r}")
        if new_name in st.patches: raise AppError(f"patch `{new_name}` already exists")
    commit_changed=(new_tree!=old_c.tree or msg!=old_c.message or desc.author.name!=old_c.author.name or desc.author.email!=old_c.author.email or desc.author.ts!=old_c.author.ts or desc.author.tz!=old_c.author.tz)
    if not commit_changed and new_name==target:
        return 0
    # check repository state if applied and current
    if target in st.applied:
        st.check_head()
        # Edit generally requires clean? Test original permits dirty for message edit top (worktree retained) likely yes. If set-tree/diff tree changes, need clean.
        if new_tree!=old_c.tree: check_clean(repo)
        else: check_no_conflicts(repo)
    trans=Transaction(st,f"edit: {target}",committer_date_is_author_date=bool(parsed.get("committer_date_is_author_date")))
    # If applied, pop above
    above=[]
    if target in st.applied:
        idx=st.applied.index(target); above=st.applied[idx+1:]
        if above: trans.pop_patches_internal(above,record=True)
    # create new commit if needed
    if commit_changed:
        parent=old_c.parents[0] if old_c.parents else None
        new_oid=create_commit(repo,new_tree,[parent] if parent else [],msg,author=desc.author,committer_date=(desc.author if parsed.get("committer_date_is_author_date") else None))
        trans.stack.patches[target]=new_oid

Pop applied patches from the lowest applied patch that is >= first selected in all order (i.e., all applied patches) if first selected is unapplied, all applied are below it in all order so none to pop? Actually applied patches are before unapplied in all order, so first selected unapplied is after all applied; no pop.
    # Determine patches to conserve: applied patches not selected that are above the highest selected applied/unapplied (?) Original pops them to push selected consecutively.
    # We'll do targeted final applied sequence:
    # If at least one selected applied: final_applied = (applied patches before first selected) + [squashed] + (applied patches after last selected not selected)
    #                           plus any selected unapplied patches are incorporated so squashed replaces them but their addition makes squashed applied (already).
    # If no selected applied: final_applied = old_applied + [squashed]? Or squashed remains unapplied at position of first selected. Choose unapplied for now.
    has_applied=any(n in old_applied for n in names_sorted)
    # Process using pop/push selected in order to create a combined patch commit at a point.
    # Steps:
    # Pop applied segment from min index among (applied patches that are at/after first selected in all order) to top.
    first_all_idx=min(allp.index(n) for n in names_sorted)
    # Applied patches to pop: those with all_idx >= first_all_idx (all selected applied and above)
    to_pop=[n for n in old_applied if allp.index(n)>=first_all_idx]
    conserved=[n for n in to_pop if n not in selected]
    if to_pop: trans.pop_patches_internal(to_pop,record=True)
    # Push selected patches in stack order
    for idx,n in enumerate(names_sorted):
        prefix=">" if idx==len(names_sorted)-1 else "+"
        ok=trans.push_one_internal(n,record_prefix=prefix)
        if not ok:
            trans.commit("squash"); return 0
    # Now selected patches are top segment applied consecutively. Combined tree = trans head tree, bottom parent = parent of first selected pushed patch commit in trans.
    combined_tree=Commit(repo,trans.stack.head).tree
    first_pushed_c=Commit(repo,trans.stack.patches[names_sorted[0]])
    combined_parent=first_pushed_c.parents[0] if first_pushed_c.parents else None
    # Pop selected segment (events?)
    # Original squash output needs probing; our events from push/pop may differ. To reduce, squash step will pop and delete other selected, modify first.
    # Pop all selected
    trans.pop_patches_internal(names_sorted,record=True)
    # Delete selected except first (which becomes squashed patch). The first patch's oid is replaced.
    squash_oid=create_commit(repo,combined_tree,[combined_parent] if combined_parent else [],msg,author=desc.author,committer_date=(desc.author if parsed.get("committer_date_is_author_date") else None))
    # remove all selected from unapplied/patches, then insert squash as applied? It will be pushed next as a patch with parent=combined_parent and tree=combined -> push fastforward.
    for n in names_sorted:
        trans.stack.unapplied=[x for x in trans.stack.unapplied if x!=n]
        trans.stack.patches.pop(n,None)
        if n!=names_sorted[0]: trans.ev(f"# {n}")
    trans.stack.patches[first]=squash_oid; trans.stack.unapplied.insert(0,first)
    trans.ev(f"& {first}")
    if new_name!=first:
        trans.stack.unapplied=[new_name if x==first else x for x in trans.stack.unapplied]
        trans.stack.patches[new_name]=trans.stack.patches.pop(first); trans.ev(f"{first} => {new_name}"); squash_name=new_name
    else: squash_name=first
    # Push squashed patch
    to_push_after=conserved
    all_to_push=[squash_name]+to_push_after
    for idx,n in enumerate(all_to_push):
        prefix=">" if idx==len(all_to_push)-1 else "+"
        ok=trans.push_one_internal(n,record_prefix=prefix)
        if not ok: break
    trans.worktree_mode="checkout"
    trans.commit("squash"); return 0

PY"}

If a branch with a StGit stack is modified with certain git commands such as
git-commit(1), git-pull(1), git-merge(1), or git-rebase(1), the StGit stack metadata
will become inconsistent with the branch state. There are a few options for resolving
this kind of situation:

1. Use 'stg undo' to undo the effect of the git commands. Or similarly use 'stg reset'
to reset the stack/branch to any previous stack state.

2. Use `stg repair`. This will repair the StGit stack metadata to accommodate the
modifications to the branch made by the git commands. Specifically, it will do the
following:

- If regular git commits were made on top of the stack of StGit patches (i.e. by using
plain `git commit`), `stg repair` will convert those commits to StGit patches,
preserving their content.

- However, merge commits cannot become patches. So if a merge was committed on top of
the stack, `stg repair` will mark all patches below the merge commit as unapplied, since
they are no longer reachable. An alternative when this is not the desired behavior is to
use `stg undo` to first get rid of the offending merge and then run `stg repair` again.

- The applied patches are supposed to be precisely those that are reachable from the
branch head. If, for example, git-reset(1) was used to move the head, some applied
patches may no longer be reachable and some unapplied patches may have become reachable.
In this case, `stg repair` will correct the applied/unapplied state of such patches.

`stg repair` will repair these inconsistencies reliably, so there are valid workflows
where git commands are used followed by `stg repair`. For example, new patches can be
created by first making commits with a graphical commit tool and then running `stg
repair` to convert those commits into patches.

Usage: stg repair [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --color <when>

          `auto` (the default) enables colored output only when outputting to a terminal
          or TTY. The `NO_COLOR` environment variable is respected.
          
          `always` and `never` unconditionlly enable/disable colored output,
          respectively.
          
          `ansi` forces color to be output using ANSI escape sequences, even in a
          Windows console.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===pull
Pull the latest changes from a remote repository.

The remote repository may be specified on the command line, but defaults to
branch.<name>.remote from the git configuration, or "origin" if not configured.

This command works by popping all currently applied patches from the stack, pulling the
changes from the remote repository, updating the stack base to the new remote HEAD, and
finally pushing all formerly applied patches back onto the stack. Merge conflicts may
occur during the final push step. Those conflicts need to be resolved manually.

See git-fetch(1) for the format of remote repository argument.

Usage: stg pull [OPTIONS] [repository]

Arguments:
  [repository]
          Repository to pull from

Options:
  -n, --nopush
          Do not push back patches after pulling

  -m, --merged
          Check for patches that may have been merged upstream.
          
          When pushing-back patches, each patch is checked to see if its changes already
          exist in the just-pulled upstream changes. If a patch's changes have already
          been merged upstream, the patch will still exist in the stack, but become
          empty after the pull operation.

      --conflicts[=<policy>]
          Either "allow" or "disallow" pushing a patch with conflicts.
          
          Using `--conflicts=allow` (or just `--conflicts`) allows pushing a patch that
          may result in unresolved merge conflicts. The patch will be pushed and files
          with conflicts will be left with conflict markers to be resolved manually; or
          the operation undone with `stg undo --hard`. This is the default behavior and
          also corresponds to the "stgit.push.allow-conflicts" variable being set to
          "true".
          
          Using `--conflicts=disallow` disallows pushing any patch that would result in
          merge conflicts. The operation will stop on the last patch that can be pushed
          without conflicts. This behavior can be configured by setting
          "stgit.push.allow-conflicts" to "false".

      --color <when>
          Specify when to colorize the output.
          
          `auto` (the default) enables colored output only when outputting to a terminal
          or TTY. The `NO_COLOR` environment variable is respected.
          
          `always` and `never` unconditionlly enable/disable colored output,
          respectively.
          
          `ansi` forces color to be output using ANSI escape sequences, even in a
          Windows console.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
===rebase
Pop all patches from the current stack, move the stack base to the given new base and
push the patches back.

Merge conflicts may arise when patches are being pushed-back onto the stack. If this
occurs, resolve the conflicts and then continue the rebase with the following sequence:

    stg add --update
    stg refresh
    stg goto top-patch

Or to skip the conflicting patch:

    stg undo --hard
    stg push next-patch..top-patch

Usage: stg rebase [OPTIONS] [committish]

Arguments:
  [committish]
          New base commit for the stack

Options:
  -i, --interactive
          Interactively manipulate patches in editor

  -n, --nopush
          Do not push back patches after rebasing

  -m, --merged
          Check for patches that may have been merged upstream.
          
          When pushing-back patches, each patch is checked to see if its changes already
          exist in the new stack base. If a patch's changes are detected to have been
          merged, the patch will still exist in the stack, but become empty after the
          rebase operation.

      --committer-date-is-author-date
          Instead of using the current time as the committer date, use the author date
          of the commit as the committer date.

      --autostash
          Automatically create a temporary stash before the operation begins, and apply
          it after the operation completes. This allows a rebase to be performed on a
          dirty work tree. Note however that the final stash application may result in
          non-trivial conflicts.

      --conflicts[=<policy>]
          Either "allow" or "disallow" pushing a patch with conflicts.
          
          Using `--conflicts=allow` (or just `--conflicts`) allows pushing a patch that
          may result in unresolved merge conflicts. The patch will be pushed and files
          with conflicts will be left with conflict markers to be resolved manually; or
          the operation undone with `stg undo --hard`. This is the default behavior and
          also corresponds to the "stgit.push.allow-conflicts" variable being set to
          "true".
          
          Using `--conflicts=disallow` disallows pushing any patch that would result in
          merge conflicts. The operation will stop on the last patch that can be pushed
          without conflicts. This behavior can be configured by setting
          "stgit.push.allow-conflicts" to "false".

  -x, --exec <cmd>
          Execute the given shell command after each patch is successfully applied
          during the rebase operation. If the command fails (exits with non-zero
          status), the entire transaction is rolled back and no patches remain applied.
          
          This option may be specified multiple times to run multiple commands in
          sequence after each patch.
          
          This is similar to `git rebase --exec`, but note that stgit rolls back the
          entire operation on failure rather than leaving you at the failing point.

      --color <when>
          Specify when to colorize the output.
          
          `auto` (the default) enables colored output only when outputting to a terminal
          or TTY. The `NO_COLOR` environment variable is respected.
          
          `always` and `never` unconditionlly enable/disable colored output,
          respectively.
          
          `ansi` forces color to be output using ANSI escape sequences, even in a
          Windows console.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

        work=f"/tmp/diff-{label}"

        outlog=[]; stepidx=0
        for step in steps:
            kind=step[0]
            stepidx+=1
            env=dict(os.environ); ts=1200000000+stepidx*100
            env.update({"GIT_AUTHOR_DATE":f"{ts} +0000","GIT_COMMITTER_DATE":f"{ts} +0000"})
            if kind=="stg":
                args=step[1]; inp=step[2] if len(step)>2 else None
                extra_env=step[3] if len(step)>3 else {}
                env.update(extra_env)
                p=subprocess.run([exe]+args,cwd=work,env=env,capture_output=True,text=True,input=inp)
                outlog.append((f"stg {args}",p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr))
            elif kind=="write":
                path,content=step[1],step[2]; mode=step[3] if len(step)>3 else "w"
                fp=os.path.join(work,path); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(fp),exist_ok=True)
                with open(fp,mode) as f: f.write(content)
            elif kind=="append":
                fp=os.path.join(work,step[1]); open(fp,"a").write(step[2])
            elif kind=="git":
                p=subprocess.run(["git"]+step[1],cwd=work,env=env,capture_output=True,text=True)
                outlog.append((f"git {step[1]}",p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr))
            elif kind=="sh":
                p=subprocess.run(step[1],shell=True,cwd=work,env=env,capture_output=True,text=True)
                outlog.append((f"sh {step[1]}",p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr))
            elif kind=="rm":
                try: os.unlink(os.path.join(work,step[1]))
                except OSError: pass
        # state snapshots using git/system only
        snaps={}

            p=subprocess.run(cmd,cwd=work,capture_output=True,text=True,shell=isinstance(cmd,str)); return (p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr)
        snaps["refs"]=snap(["git","for-each-ref"])
        snaps["status"]=snap(["git","status","-s"])
        snaps["stackjson"]=snap("git cat-file -p refs/stacks/master:stack.json 2>/dev/null || true")
        snaps["log"]=snap("git log --first-parent --format='%s' refs/stacks/master 2>/dev/null || true")
        snaps["headcommit"]=snap("git log -1 --format='%T %P %an %ae %at %cn %ce %ct %s' HEAD 2>/dev/null || true")
        files={}
        for root,dirs,fnames in os.walk(work):
            if ".git" in root.split(os.sep): continue
            dirs[:]=[d for d in dirs if d!=".git"]
            for fn in fnames:
                fp=os.path.join(root,fn); rel=os.path.relpath(fp,work); files[rel]=pathlib.Path(fp).read_bytes()
        snaps["files"]=files
        results[label]=(outlog,snaps)
    ok=True
    ref_log,new_log=results["ref"][0],results["new"][0]
    for a,b in zip(ref_log,new_log):
        if a!=b:
            ok=False; print(f"\n[{name}] OUTPUT DIFF at {a[0]}:\n REF exit={a[1]} out={a[2]!r} err={a[3]!r}\n NEW exit={b[1]} out={b[2]!r} err={b[3]!r}")
    for key in results["ref"][1]:

    return ok

cat > /tmp/replace_fold.py << 'PY'
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('/workspace/src/__main__.py'); s=p.read_text(); start=s.index('def cmd_fold(args):'); end=s.index('def cmd_spill(args):')
new=r'''def cmd_fold(args):
    opts=[Opt("threeway",long="--threeway",short="t"),Opt("base",long="--base",short="b",value_name="<committish>"),Opt("strip",long="--strip",short="p",value_name="<n>",validator=v_int),Opt("context",short="C",value_name="<n>",validator=v_int),Opt("reject",long="--reject"),color_opt()]
    pos=[Pos("file","[file]",minv=0,maxv=1)]
    spec=Spec("fold",options=opts,positionals=pos)
    parsed=parse_args(spec,args); repo=open_repo(); st=Stack.open(repo)
    if not st.applied: raise AppError("no patches applied")
    st.check_head(); check_no_conflicts(repo)
    idx,_wt=index_and_worktree_dirty(repo)
    if idx: raise AppError("index not clean; use `refresh` or `reset --hard`")
    fname=parsed.get("file")
    if fname is None or fname=="-":
        diff_text=sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode('utf-8','surrogateescape')
    else:
        try: diff_text=Path(fname).read_text(encoding='utf-8',errors='surrogateescape')
        except FileNotFoundError: raise AppError("No such file or directory (os error 2)")
    strip=parsed.get("strip") if parsed.get("strip") is not None else 1
    if parsed.get("threeway") or parsed.get("base"):
        if parsed.get("base"):
            base_oid=repo.rev_parse(parsed.get("base")) or rev_resolve(repo,st,parsed.get("base"))
            base_tree=Commit(repo,base_oid).tree
        else:
            top_c=st.patch_commit(st.top()); base_tree=top_c.parent_tree()
        result_tree=apply_diff_to_tree(repo,base_tree,diff_text,strip=strip)
        curr_tree=Commit(repo,st.head).tree
        result,conflicts=merge_trees(repo,base_tree,curr_tree,result_tree)
        if conflicts:
            apply_merge_conflicts(repo,result,conflicts,curr_tree)
            for ln in conflict_status_lines(repo,conflicts): out(ln+"\n")
            raise ConflictError()
        merged_tree=tree_from_map(repo,result)
        # Update index+worktree to merged tree (relative to HEAD, so changes are staged)
        p=git_out("read-tree","-u","-m",curr_tree,merged_tree)
        if p.returncode!=0: git_out("read-tree","-u","--reset",merged_tree)
        return 0
    apply_args=["apply","--index",f"-p{strip}"]
    if parsed.get("context") is not None: apply_args.append(f"-C{parsed.get('context')}")
    if parsed.get("reject"): apply_args += ["--reject","--verbose"]
    p=git_out(*apply_args,inp=diff_text)
    if p.returncode!=0:
        giterr=p.stderr.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape')
        if parsed.get("reject"):
            err_out("info: `git apply --index`: "+giterr)
            raise AppError("patch conflicts",code=3)
        raise AppError(f"`git apply --index`: {giterr.rstrip()}")
    return 0

'''
p.write_text(s[:start]+new+s[end:])
PY
